description: Given the head of a linked list, delete the middle node (floor(n/2)-th node, 0-indexed) and return the modified head.
examples:
Input: head = [1,3,4,7,1,2,6]
Output: [1,3,4,1,2,6]
Explanation: The middle node (index 3, value 7) is removed.
intuition: The slow/fast pointer technique finds the middle of a linked list in one pass. By starting fast slightly ahead, slow ends up right before the middle node, making deletion a simple pointer reassignment.
approach: Use slow and fast pointers. Fast moves 2 steps, slow moves 1 step. When fast reaches the end, slow is at the middle. Use a prev pointer to delete the middle node.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: head = [1,3,4,7,1,2,6] (n=7, middle index=3 -> value 7)
slow=node(1), fast=node(4) (head.next.next)
Iter 1: fast=node(4),fast.next=node(7) -> slow=node(3), fast=node(1)
Iter 2: fast=node(1),fast.next=node(2) -> slow=node(4), fast=node(6)
Iter 3: fast=node(6),fast.next=null -> stop
slow=node(4), slow.next=node(7)
slow.next = node(7).next = node(1)
List becomes: [1,3,4,1,2,6]
explanation:
1. If the list has 0 or 1 node, return None.
2. Initialize slow at head, fast at head.next.next.
3. Move slow 1 step and fast 2 steps until fast reaches the end.
4. Now slow is the node before the middle.
5. Delete the middle by setting slow.next = slow.next.next.
hints: Use the classic slow/fast pointer technique.
Start fast one step ahead so slow ends up before the middle.
Handle edge cases: single node or two nodes.
